sections.overview: The World Spider Catalog accepts Ero aphana in the pirate-spider family Mimetidae.
sections.identification: Males are about 2.5 mm and females 3.0–4.2 mm; four humps mark the abdomen, but genitalia help separate similar Ero.
sections.habitat: It occurs on bushes in warm areas, including woodland edges; French records also include other vegetation and rocky places.
sections.diet: Mimetids prey on other web-building spiders, invading webs before attacking.
sections.behavior: The French regional account describes mimetids approaching on the host web and seizing prey with spiny forelegs.
sections.reproduction: ODIN reports an annual cycle, spring-to-summer adults and suspended egg sacs with up to about ten eggs.
sections.ecology: Four abdominal humps distinguish it from several Ero with two; genital examination helps separate E. tuberculata.
sections.conservation: The French regional platform lists Least Concern in Normandy; this is a regional, not global, assessment.
